## Goal

The decisive feature: one command that tells a blind agent, in stable JSON, whether its artifact builds, renders, works and still does what it did last time.

## Owned requirements

Close each with the check below, through the real public interface (README §3).

| ID | Requirement | Route | Concrete check |
|---|---|---|---|
| AX-02 | `verify` runs the full pipeline in ARCHITECTURE §12 and returns one JSON verdict | I, B | Pipeline stage fixtures each produce their diagnostics; verdict validates; timings recorded |
| AX-04 | `verify` detects regressions against the last passing version | I | Regression fixture (removed control, layout shift, missing field) detected against the last passing version |
| AX-05 | Screenshots default to DPR 1, carry token estimates and are returned only on failure or request | M | Screenshots at DPR 1 with token estimates; images returned only on failure or request |
| AU-05 | Every persisted input has a stable field ID; `verify` reports missing or duplicate IDs | M, B | Fixtures with duplicate IDs, IDs changing between renders and unbound controls produce MOSTRA_FIELD_* codes at the right severity |
| VR-09 | Publish reuses the cached verify verdict for the exact source and environment digests or runs verify; errors refuse publish; `--force` publishes and records the failing codes | I | Publish reuses a cached verdict (no rebuild), refuses on errors, and with --force records failing codes in the manifest |

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- the verify runner child with a warm Chromium;
- the pipeline stages of ARCHITECTURE §12;
- field-ID lint;
- the smoke test with the dry-run contract;
- ARIA and pixel regressions against the last passing version;
- screenshot token estimates and the image-return rule;
- the cached verdict and the publish gate with `--force`.

Design detail for this package:

- From WP-08 (D129 to D133): a dry run is a plain call with `dryRun: true` in the worker call's context (`CallContext.dryRun`, `worker/call`); the worker's `dryRun()` reads it. `registry.json`'s `actions[].dryRun` says which exports opted in. `verify` clears a parked worker of the artifact (`pool.clear`, as a publish does). Extend the RT-02 audit (`test/integration/audit.test.ts`, which WP-08 extended to calls, runs and live sources) to verify runs.
- From WP-07 (D109, D111): `registry.json` has `fields` (`{ open, openReasons, entries }`, `packages/runtime/src/builder/child/fields.ts`), the static scan AU-05's duplicate and changing-ID checks start from; the target `verify` (`<meta name="mostra-target" content="verify">`) routes with browser history like `live`, and `mountArtifact` and `mountRoutes` report `mostra/ready` once the runtime's first snapshot arrived (or after 3 s), which verify waits on.
- Stages in order with early exit on compile failure; warm browser in the verify runner child.
- Severity rule from D72: smoke observations without a runtime error are warnings; hover-opened and already-active controls classified before judging; never click through actions that didn't opt into `dryRun()`.
- Regression baseline: the last passing version's ARIA snapshot, pixels and contracts (fields, actions, live sources).
- Cached verdict by source and env digest; publish gate with `--force` recording codes.
- Screenshot token estimates for Claude, GPT and Gemini formulas (brief 6).
- Readiness: boot and render wait on the Mostra readiness signal and server health, never on fixed sleeps (EVAL-01b found a start-up race in a sleep-based checker).
- Run `verify` on WP-03's AU-01 and AU-02 fixtures and extend its RT-02 process audit to verify runs; regression baselines come from the last passing version stored in the home (its build and `registry.json`), never from the authoring directory (VR-11, D93).
- Verify resolves packages exactly as publish does, through WP-04's `Dependencies.resolve` with the same working-lockfile key (D95), so its cached verdict's `envDigest` (which includes `lockDigest`) matches the publish that follows; `MOSTRA_DEP_*` diagnostics are compile-phase verdict entries.

## Acceptance evidence

fixture artifacts for each diagnostic phase produce their codes; a non-opted action is never invoked; a regression fixture is detected; verdict JSON validates against the schema; publish is refused on errors and recorded with `--force`.

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- False positives make agents break working code (EVAL-01): every new check needs a negative fixture proving it doesn't fire on correct code.

## Handoff

Agents can iterate to `pass` and publish safely.
